items.label: Blind
items.title: Blind policy, unseen pegs of the training family
items.text: The policy slides the peg on the plate until it feels the hole, then it drops the peg in. The rare failures do not find the hole in 5 s or push the peg off the plate.

items.label: Wrist RGB
items.title: Wrist-camera policy, unseen pegs of the training family
items.text: The visual policy moves almost directly to the hole. It is faster than the blind policy on familiar parts.

items.label: RGB, tighter fit
items.title: Wrist-camera policy, tighter clearance (held out)
items.text: With 0.5 to 0.6 mm clearance, the visual policy often stops partly inside the hole. The blind policy seats 97% of the same parts.

items.label: Blind, extreme size
items.title: Blind policy, extreme part sizes (held out)
items.text: Very small and very large parts. Most failures leave the plate or do not find the hole.

items.label: Blind, random convex
items.title: Blind policy, random convex shapes (held out)
items.text: These shapes have corners that the training pegs do not have. The peg often slips in the grasp or stops partly inside the hole.

items.label: Spiral search
items.title: Scripted spiral search with the true hole position
items.text: The spiral covers the area around the hole in circles. It moves much farther than the learned policies.

items.label: Unseen gear sets
items.title: Blind gear policy, unseen gear sets
items.text: The policy slides the gear down the shaft and turns it until the teeth mesh with the anchor gears.

items.label: Random tooth shape
items.title: Blind gear policy, random tooth shapes (held out)
items.text: The tooth shapes are different from training. The policy meshes them as well.

items.label: 1-step latency
items.title: YAM peg policy with 20 ms of latency it did not train with
items.text: Old mount (fixture below the base); the lab-table runs show the same result. The policy overshoots and pushes the peg off the plate or past the hole.

items.label: 1 arcmin backlash
items.title: YAM peg policy with backlash it did not train with
items.text: Old mount. With a small dead zone in each joint, the policy often does not find the hole.

items.label: Final stage
items.title: USB-C, final stage: 0.02 to 0.1 mm clearance, 3 mm median start
items.text: Lab-table mount. The policy presses the plug on the housing and searches in small steps. Most failures start far from the port and do not find it in 8 s.

items.label: Far starts
items.title: USB-C, starts up to 9 mm from the port, 0.05 mm clearance
items.text: The capture radius is approximately 6 mm. Starts farther away usually time out.

items.label: 1-step latency
items.title: USB-C policy with 20 ms of latency it did not train with
items.text: Success decreases from 78% to 5%. The search becomes unstable and the drive slips or leaves the housing.

items.label: Chamfered port
items.title: USB-C, port with a 0.2 to 0.5 mm lead-in (not in training)
items.text: The lead-in guides the plug. The policy that never saw a chamfer seats more drives than without it.

items.label: Latch
items.title: USB-C, latch spring of 5 to 15 N over the last 1.5 mm (not in training)
items.text: The policy does not push hard enough. The drive slips in the grasp or stays partly inside.

items.label: Side port
items.title: USB-C, port facing the robot (port-up policy, not trained for it)
items.text: The arm pose is different, so the port-up policy moves the plug off the housing. This task needs its own training.
